content:
Just outside the gates of Nuevo Laredo's Panteón Municipal Antiguo, one woman has spent 17 years helping families say goodbye in color. Lorena García makes her living crafting floral arrangements for the Day of the Dead — and with the celebrations just days away, her busiest season is now underway, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo.

Her stand sits near the cemetery entrance, stocked with artificial-flower arrangements, wreaths with or without religious images, and small teddy-bear and puppy figures. She reserves special tenderness for arrangements honoring children who died young — the "angelitos," as she calls them — a quiet way of standing with grieving families during the Day of the Dead celebrations, the paper reports.

Prices run from 50 to 1,200 pesos depending on size, materials and design, so there is something for every budget. García says sales started picking up this week, but the real rush will hit Oct. 31 and Nov. 1–2. She has run her own business for nine of her 17 years in the trade.

Visitors are already arriving, she told the paper — some from other cities, other states, and even the United States, where they have loved ones resting here. She invited the whole community to stop by: her stand is right by the cemetery entrance, open to all comers.
